Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 398 - 12 (Roll no. 235). (text: CR H4395-4396)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 8897.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H4395-4396)

dimensions.assessment: Affects adult passengers traveling with children aged 12 and under, airport security personnel, and TSA staff at selected pilot airports.
dimensions.evidence: expedite access to security screening for adult passengers and accompanying child passengers twelve years of age and under

dimensions.assessment: Creates an optional pilot program at a minimum of five airports prioritizing high-volume locations, without altering mandatory security protocols.
dimensions.evidence: establish a pilot program at airports to expedite access to security screening... at a minimum of five airports

dimensions.assessment: Utilizes existing TSA personnel and resource reallocations without stating new funding appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: Permit local Administration management to open or close checkpoint lanes and reallocate available resources as needed

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes a targeted pilot program and congressional briefing requirements for airport security screening procedures.
dimensions.evidence: Administrator of the Transportation Security Administration... may establish a pilot program at airports

dimensions.assessment: Operates as a pilot program for a duration of two years, with a briefing required within 270 days of establishment.
dimensions.evidence: carry out such pilot program for a period of two years

missing_information: Which specific airports will be selected for the pilot program.
Exact operational costs associated with alternative screening lanes.
importance_detail.rationale: Authorizes the TSA to establish a two-year pilot program at a minimum of five airports providing alternative security screening for passengers traveling with children aged 12 and under.
